ctx.x: But I -- he never knew how old the classical guitar was until I started studying with him, and so I was there taking a lesson one day, and an old black man came in, this guy looked like he was about 80. He was -- well, he was in his eighties. Very stately and well groomed, and he and Mr. Lanham started talking and it was very interesting to hear them talk. They had toured Europe. I forgot this guy's name, playing the classical guitar. Years before. Now this was in the thirties, you know, and I was amazed, because…
He also taught I think this guy's name is Albert Pick, who was -- he's quite a guitarist, he's quite a classical

guitarist. And he lives in Chicago, but at this time that he was teaching Pick he was trying to get me to take classical guitar. But I was working with Roy at the time, at the Three Duces, and I wasn't interested. You know, I was thinking of jazz then you know. I was working with Zuty and all of the-- the real jazz men. And that was -- I just went to him, for musicianship, really, you know.
